plugins.name: Feeds
plugins.summary: Bluesky and X timelines on your glasses.
plugins.description: Read your social feeds on the HUD. Bluesky needs no account; X connects through an in-app sign-in. Threads, images, and swipe navigation, rendered as structured cards.
plugins.author: alvarosw

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Read your social feeds on the HUD. Bluesky needs no account; X connects through an in-app sign-in. Threads, images, and swipe navigation, rendered as structured cards.

releases.notes:
- Live grid tile (optional `widget_tile` capability, all seven tile sizes): up
  to six posts of the default timeline with author, handle, text, media marker
  and age, and a "N new" summary. Fetched once when the hub's tile lease starts
  and once per hub refresh, never on a timer of the plugin's own. X (WebView)
  is never used for the tile; with that default the tile reads Bluesky.
- The layout editor previews the tile with sample posts until a real one is
  published.

plugins.name: Lyrics
plugins.description: Synced lyrics that follow whatever is playing on your phone. Spotify sign-in for synced lines, with LrcLib and Netease fallbacks. Opens itself when a track starts, if you let it.
plugins.author: alvarosw

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Synced lyrics that follow whatever is playing on your phone. Spotify sign-in for synced lines, with LrcLib and Netease fallbacks. Opens itself when a track starts, if you let it.

releases.notes:
- Live grid tile (optional `widget_tile` capability, all seven tile sizes):
  synced lyrics as a window of timed lines that the glasses advance with the
  playback position, unsynced lyrics from the top, and the track title when no
  lyrics are found. Published per track, seek, play/pause, or when playback
  nears the end of the published window, never per line.
- The media session is followed for the tile only while the hub's tile lease
  is active; closing the surface no longer stops it while the lease holds.
- The layout editor previews the tile with sample lyrics until a real one is
  published.

plugins.name: Media Deck
plugins.summary: Now playing and transport controls on the HUD.

plugins.author: alvarosw

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

Whatever plays on your phone shows on the glasses: title, artist, artwork, and progress. Tap to play or pause, swipe to skip. Audio never passes through Nexus.

releases.notes:
- Live grid tile (optional `widget_tile` capability, all seven tile sizes): the
  playing track's title, artist, album, source app, position and cover, published
  on a track change, play/pause, a seek or a late cover, and "Nothing playing"
  when no media session is active. The media session is watched only while the
  hub's tile lease is active; the plugin stays dormant otherwise.
- The layout editor previews the tile with a sample track until a real one is
  published.

plugins.name: News
plugins.summary: RSS and Atom feeds on the HUD, read with the ring.
plugins.description: Subscribe to RSS or Atom feeds on the phone and read them on the glasses: sources with unread counts, headlines newest first, and the article text on the glasses' native reader surface. Fully operable with the R08 ring.
plugins.author: alvarosw

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

News puts your RSS and Atom feeds on the Rokid glasses. Subscribe on the phone, then browse headlines and read articles on the HUD without touching anything but the ring.

- Three views on one axis: sources, headlines, reader. Forward/back moves, tap opens, double tap goes back.
- Headlines use both text bands of a list row, with age and source as trailing tokens; read items dim instead of disappearing.
- Article text is reduced to paragraphs on the phone and rendered on the glasses' native reader surface: continuous prose that the ring scrolls, opening on the first paragraph.
- Per-feed unread counts, cached articles between sessions, and a feed that fails to fetch keeps what it had.
- Add feeds by URL or from seven verified presets (BBC World, NYT World, Hacker News, Ars Technica, The Verge, G1, Tecnoblog); each feed names itself from its channel title on the first fetch.

Requests only the `surfaces` capability: feeds are fetched phone-side with the app's own HTTP stack.

releases.notes:
- **A live tile for the glasses grid** (optional `widget_tile` capability, all
  seven tile sizes `1x1` to `3x3`): the newest unread headlines, up to six, in up
  to three sections, one per outlet with its unread count. Each item carries the
  headline, the outlet, the opening of its summary and its age; the header reads
  `N unread` (`N` on a one-column tile) and the rest count as "+N more".
- The tile is refresh-driven and lives only inside the hub's tile lease: one
  fetch of every feed when the lease starts and one per hub refresh, then idle.
  News schedules no refresh of its own. A refresh within a minute of the last
  fetch republishes from the cache, so what was read in the plugin leaves the
  tile without a second fetch.
- The tile's fetch refreshes the cache the plugin opens on; a fetch no feed
  answered keeps showing the cached headlines and leaves the cache's age alone.
- The phone's layout editor previews the tile with a sample until a real one is
  published (`TILE_PREVIEW`).
- Built against the live tiles SDK from the `alvarosw/Rokid-Nexus` fork
  (`ed7ca9a1c4`) instead of `sdk-v0.15.0`; no other behavior changes. Because
  `widget_tile` is optional, the APK still loads on a hub without tiles; on a hub
  with them, the new capability asks for re-approval once.
- Releases from the fork are signed with the fork's certificate
  (`78a1be10…5f56d60`), so moving from an upstream build needs a reinstall.


### Artifact

- File: `news-phone-release.apk`
- SHA-256: `04acf95088d4145608877bd3c5d5f5cec71ad885c0941655de09da99777e2dde`
- Signer SHA-256: `78a1be1045ba3b2614baa46e306a353a8a6bc3e5d07ba5d587490931d5f56d60`

plugins.name: Relay
plugins.summary: Phone messages on your glasses, answered out loud.
plugins.description: A message you can reply to reaches the glasses as it arrives. Read it without taking the phone out, speak your answer, and it sends itself. Anything you miss waits for you in Messages.
plugins.author: alvarosw

listing.descriptionMarkdown:
## About

A message you can reply to reaches the glasses as it arrives, and lights the display if it was dark. You read it where you are already looking, answer out loud, and the phone stays in your pocket.

## Reading

Each message keeps its sender beside it, so a group conversation reads as a conversation rather than a wall of text. A long thread turns pages instead of stopping at eight lines.

*Message display time* in the plugin's settings is a number you type, 2 to 45 seconds, and *Longer for long messages* adds reading time per character on top for threads that need it.

## Privacy

In public or in a meeting, *Hide message text on the glasses* keeps the band to the sender's name and a Show chip — the words appear only when you tap for them, and Reply stays one tap away. *Hide previews in the inbox* does the same for the Messages list. While the band is hidden, read-aloud names the sender only.

## Answering

Speak your reply and it sends itself after a few seconds, counted down on the chip you are looking at — cancellable for its whole length, and never sent before you have seen what it heard. If the glasses went dark or lost the link, the clock stops and waits for you.

Prefer to type? Tap *Type* once dictation has started, or turn on *Reply by typing* in the plugin's settings to skip dictation altogether. With Rokid Nexus 1.4.13 the notice itself becomes the reply field: what you type appears under the message as you type it, and the phone keyboard opens on its own, then closes when you send. A keyboard paired to the glasses works too. Enter sends it through the same steps.

## Messages you missed

One you let go, or one that arrived while you were in another plugin, is in **Messages** in the Nexus menu: every conversation waiting on you, newest first, read and answered the same way. The list updates while you are looking at it.

## Hearing it instead

Turn on *Read notifications aloud* and the glasses speak the message as it arrives — the whole message, in the voice and at the speed you already chose in your Rokid assistant settings. It is produced on the glasses, so it works with the phone in your pocket and nothing leaves the device. Off by default.

## What it relays

Anything with a reply box, from any app. Nothing else, and nothing to tick first.

## What it keeps

Nothing. Messages live in memory while the plugin runs, are never written to disk, and never appear in a log. Revoke notification access and what it captured goes with it.

## Needs

Rokid Nexus 1.4.11 or newer on both phone and glasses; 1.4.13 to type inside the notice.

Notification access on the phone, plus *Show on your glasses*, *Speech to text* and *Text to speech* in Nexus → Settings → Plugin access.

releases.notes:
- **Live grid tile** (optional `widget_tile` capability, all seven tile sizes):
  the inbox's conversations with sender, app, newest message, age and initials
  under an "N new" summary, republished as messages arrive, are removed or are
  answered. The inbox is read for the tile only while the hub's tile lease is
  active. Conversations Android redacted never appear on it, and the hide
  switches hide the message text there too.
- The layout editor previews the tile with sample conversations until a real
  one is published.
- **One bus registration.** The notice band now talks through the plugin
  service's own connection instead of opening a second one under the same id,
  so a band, the inbox and the tile lease can overlap without the hub losing
  track of Relay.
